#1999. Hull City v Brighton and Hove Albion: Unity between contrasting groups key to Tigers' success

Last season, Hull won promotion via the Championship play-offs on the back of a squad who has been the course and distance in the division.

That group was put together under restrictions which stopped Hull buying or even paying a loan fee for players in 2025-26. With the restrictions lifted and a ticket for the gravy train that is the world's most lucrative domestic football league, they have broadened their horizons.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Eighteen players were signed – although Joe Gelhardt was a loan made permanent – and are overwhelmingly young and new to English football.

Yet according to 22-year-old Cho – who spent his childhood flitting between England and France – as well as performing brilliantly in the season’s first ten games, the old guard have welcomed the next generation.

It is why Hull go into Sunday's Premier League game at home to Brighton and Hove Albion still unbeaten on the banks of the Humber this season. Whoever pulled on the black and amber, the Tigers simply would not be able to compete if their squad was fractured.

"The lads that were here before, they've been amazing with the new lads," says the French-born player in an English accent which shows why he has represented both countries in international age-group football.

"I don't think there's two groups. Everyone's joking with everyone, everyone's working with everyone.

"It does say a lot (about the mainly British and Irish players who were at the club last season). Then again, it's football and we're at a high level, so everyone knows there's going to be a lot of competition.

"The main thing is just being as good as you can to each other off the pitch and then when we're on the pitch as competitive as possible.

"I feel that's a really important strength because that's what's got us here so far. I feel like we need to keep that until the end of the season."

Not all of the new signings came speaking good English, so Cho's bilingualism is important.

"I've got a few of the French players I'm pretty close to," he says. "Lucas Gourna (a team-mate in the French age-group teams) speaks fairly good English so it's not too much of a problem with him.

"But Nobel (Mendy) and Robinio (Vaz), they don't speak that good English so sometimes you have to help them out.

"I've got my family not too far from here in Manchester so that's been really helpful, and some of my team-mates live really close by so we always go to each other's (homes) and just chill with each other.

"It's really important off the pitch what you do to be good on the pitch."

If Cho's off-field role is clear, on the field it has been less so.

He may not have had the language barrier to hurdle, but he has had many of the problems his team-mates did joining late in the transfer window, in his case because of what he calls a "roller-coaster" of an on-off transfer. Coach Sergej Jakirovic thinks he has still not yet caught up.

"He's a very quick player so he can run behind," explains Jakirovic. "Maybe sometimes he can better cover the ball, to save the ball (keep possession), at least to win a foul.

"It's also about fitness because his recovery after sprinting is still too long. In his last club (Nice), he was removed from training because he was waiting for a transfer. Ten days he didn't train with the team.

"Now he's healthy, thank God, and everything's on him (to perform)."

Hull have largely used Cho from the bench as a right winger but their best player, Mohamed Belloumi – one of the younger members of the old guard – plays there too. Their next best, Oli McBurnie, is a centre-forward, his other position.

So it was significant for Cho that Jakirovic switched from 5-4-1 to 5-3-2 at Arsenal, giving Cho a first Premier League start alongside McBurnie.

"I need to keep working and stay ready," says Cho, who picked up a minor injury on the back of his first goal. "Wherever the coach wants me to play, I'm just trying to be as helpful as I can to the team.

"(Arsenal) was a great experience. I knew it was going to be tough even before the game.

"But Iit was just trying to make advantage of my colleagues by getting in behind, trying to hurt the opponents with my runs in behind and trying to be a threat every time we had the ball in transition.

"I know I can do better, we can do better as a team always but I feel like there's a lot to take from it."

Manchester United could push for Villarreal full-back Alex Freeman in January, a player Mauricio Pochettino has tipped to become ‘one of the best in the world’ in his position.

Pochettino was confirmed as Michael Carrick’s successor last week and will arrive in Manchester today ahead of his first game in charge away to Liverpool this weekend.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager will be backed in the January transfer window with a striker and a full-back thought to be priorities.

#1997. Huddersfield Town v Leicester City: Drury's vow regarding Sanches Fernandes plus empathy for Foxes rival

They can also rest assured that the talismanic winger will not get carried away - or 'giddy' as they say in these parts.

Footage of Fernandes cutting inside from the position he loves on the right flank before unleashing a sweet left-foot drive into the net - just 15 minutes into his bow for the Blue Sharks - did the rounds late last week.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The 25-year-old came off the bench in the final quarter of the Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against Liberia and was afforded a memorable moment in his burgeoning career.

Unfortunately, a bout of gastroenteritis ensured that Fernandes did not feature in the second leg of the double-header on Tuesday. After returning to the UK early, he is now over his sickness bug and in the reckoning for today's juicy fixture.

On the recognition, head coach Martin Drury said: "I think it's nothing less than he deserves for the level of performance he's put in this season. Not just with the ball, but without the ball.

"I think he's been outstanding. You see the goal he scores, he comes on the pitch for 15 minutes and does what I see him doing in training every day and what we've seen him doing in the league.

"So, full credit to him. But I think the big thing with him is he's so level-headed. He doesn't go there and get carried away with it. He uses it for what he needs to use it for in terms of his development and his learning.

"I'm sure he'll become a better player and person as a result of that experience."

Town face a Leicester side who are starting to make their move in third-tier circles after a tough start to the campaign which saw head coach Russell Martin receive no end of vitriol on social media platforms in particular.

Drury remains a big fan of his work, although he will not want to see too much evidence of it today.

Regarding how Martin blanked out the 'noise' early in the season, the Town chief is full of respect.

He continued: "In the industry that we live in, there's a platform for people to say whatever they want. And when it's really positive, that can be really good. When it's not positive, sometimes we just have to remember we're talking about human beings here.

"Football coaches and football players aren't abnormal; they're human beings. And I've seen some of the stuff that he's had labelled his way.

"I'm not sat here saying he's perfect, he's doing everything right. But I can only speak from a coaching point of view and personal view, having met him. He's a really good human being. I think he's a really talented coach.

"I've got a lot of respect for him - for the fact that he's got the mental strength to deal with that. And I think he's got an inner belief in himself that the work that he does is good."

#1996. Ashley Young names Premier League star Manchester United should sign to replace Bruno Fernandes

Ashley Young reckons it is time for Manchester United to move on from Bruno Fernandes and feels there is a Premier League star who should be signed to replace him.

Fernandes has consistently been the Red Devils’ best player since joining from Sporting in January 2020.

However, at 32 years old and with new manager Mauricio Pochettino arriving this week, doubts over whether Fernandes will remain the focal point of the team are being raised.

The United captain is into the final few months of his contract and has reportedly rejected two offers of a new deal.

The club has the option to extend his current contract by another month, which would prevent Fernandes leaving on a free transfer in the summer, but he could still be sold in 2027 if that option is taken up.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Former Red Devils man Young reckons it is time to move on from Fernandes and thinks the man to replace him is Nottingham Forest and England midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White.

The former Wolves star turns 27 in January and Young feels now is the time for Manchester United to make him their main man, replacing Fernandes.

‘He’s been unbelievable for the club, the standout performer,’ Young said of Fernandes on Overlap Daily. ‘But there’s been so much that’s come about. He’s turned down another contract, we’re hearing.

‘You want to build around a player. He’s 33 next year. Age is nothing but a number, but he’s not in his peak. I wouldn’t say past it, but he’s getting older now.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘For me, I would go and sign Morgan Gibbs-White. I’m just throwing that name out there. But you’re thinking a number 10 and you want to build a team around a player.

‘He’s young, he’s hungry, he’s just got in the England squad. I think he’s got the capabilities to go and play for – no disrespect to Nottingham Forest – a bigger club. And I think he’s someone that Manchester United need, in his peak years.

‘I think he’s shown more than enough at Nottingham Forest to be able to go and say I can play for a bigger club like Manchester United and take the weight of that.’

As much as signing new players will be on the agenda for the new Manchester United manager, getting rid of unwanted squad members may be the bigger test.

Gary Neville feels there needs to be a significant cull over the next few transfer windows, with some big names ideally being axed at the end of the season.

‘If you look through it now I’d say Martinez would go, [Matthijs] De Ligt would go, [Noussair] Mazraoui would go, [Mason] Mount would go, first wave next summer. [Marcus] Rashford if you can, and [Joshua] Zirkzee,’ the former full-back said on Stick to United.

‘And then the year after you’d be looking at [Luke] Shaw, [Harry] Maguire, [Diogo] Dalot, Bruno [Fernandes], that’s your second wave and maybe then you’ve made your mind up on [Carlos] Baleba and [Andrey] Santos.

‘But the earliest Mauricio Pochettino can unravel this squad is two seasons if he does well. It could take three to get this squad unravelled.’

#1995. Man United transfer news: Red Devils 'suffer blow' in pursuit of Fulham star ahead of January market

By Matt Law | 19 Nov 2026 20:03, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:05

Fulham are reportedly working to extend Calvin Bassey's contract amid interest from Manchester United.

The Red Devils are expected to bring a centre-back to Old Trafford in the January transfer window due to their problems in that area of the field.

Man United are planning to overhaul their defensive unit next summer, as Lisandro Martinez, Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw are all out of contract, while there is speculation surrounding the futures of Matthijs de Ligt, Noussair Mazraoui and Diogo Dalot.

However, due to the team's severe defensive problems this term, it is likely that a new centre-back will be targeted when the winter window opens for business.

Man United have conceded 19 times in their 10 Premier League matches this season, which is the joint-third worst record in the division.

The Red Devils have actually not kept a single clean sheet in the Premier League this term, while they have also conceded eight times in their four Champions League matches.

Bassey has allegedly been identified by Man United as a leading target, with the 26-year-old's contract due to expire at the end of the campaign.

Fulham do have the option to activate another year on the Nigeria international's deal, but the club are looking to sign him to a long-term contract.

According to The Athletic, Fulham are currently pushing to extend his deal, with the London team having no intention of letting him leave in the winter market.

Bassey has captained Fulham this season, making 12 appearances in 2026-27, while he has represented the club on 113 occasions in all competitions.

The defender has also played for Rangers and Ajax during his professional career.

Bassey gained Champions League experience during his time at Ajax, while he has now played 104 times in the Premier League for Fulham, scoring three goals and registering one assist.

New Man United head coach Mauricio Pochettino is expected to be backed with funds during the January transfer window.

#1994. Gomes scores for Aston Villa in defeat by Bayern Munich in Hong Kong

Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.

Bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick. Villa goalkeeper Marco Bizot made a string of saves in the second half to keep Bayern’s lead at one goal until former Liverpool forward Luis Díaz smashed in Bayern’s second off the underside of the bar.

Just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side showed some life late on. Summer signing João Gomes’s goal from the edge of the box gave them hope before Tammy Abraham nearly brought them back onto level terms, only to be denied by a fine save from 40-year-old Manuel Neuer.

Aston Villa are next in action in six days’ time when they take on Paris St-Germain in the Uefa Super Cup before kicking off their Premier League campaign at Brighton. Bayern have one more friendly to come against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

Stepping up in the big moments! 🐐🧤 pic.twitter.com/r14rF39XpR

Unai Emery’s men head home from the Far East to face PSG in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg next week and then have one more pre-season friendly against Borussia Monchengladbach before starting their Premier League campaign at Brighton.

Possession: Aston Villa 44%-56% Bayern MunichShots: 8-16Shots on target: 3-8Corners: 3-7

Bizot nearly has a calamitous moment coming out of his penalty area but gets away with it.

The final whistle is blown soon after and Bayern hold on to beat Villa 2-1 in Hong Kong. They had looked comfortable when Diaz put them 2-0 up but Villa kept going until the end.

Victory in the final match of the #AudiFCBTour! 💪🔥 pic.twitter.com/UFhQhme62i

The space opens up for Palhinha to shoot from range but Bizot makes a fairly comfortable save down to his right.

It was all Bayern for 80 minutes of this game but Villa have come to life in the closing stages, with Vincent Kompany’s side now holding on a bit.

When Diaz scored Bayern’s second goal, Aston Villa were out of this game but it has been all Villa since then. They look the more likely to get a goal.

Gomes’ free-kick out on the left is parried behind by Neuer for a Villa corner on the right. The corner comes to nothing.

For 80 minutes, Aston Villa barely looked like scoring but come so close to getting two goals in just a few minutes. Abraham meets a cross from the right and must think he has scored but his header is brilliantly saved by the 40-year-old Neuer.

Maybe this game is not quite done and dusted yet. A cross from the right picks out Gomes on the edge of the box. The Brazilian takes one touch before toe poking past Neuer and into the Bayern net. Gomes meant that finish and Villa have some hope.

Abraham should have done better there. He has the space to drive down Villa’s right and has a decision to make; cross the ball to his left and drive forward himself to shoot. He takes a while to make the decision before his attempted cross is intercepted by Ito.

Boey’s yellow card was his final act of the game as he is replaced by Della Rovere. Boey did seem to be struggling with some cramp.

Bayern receive their second yellow card of the game as Boey is booked for cynically pulling down Lynch.

Cash, Maatsen and Buendia have gone off for Aston Villa.

Double substitution from Bayern as Pavic and Assomo replace Tah and Brown.

A fantastic goal to put the Germans 2-0 up and it is nothing more than they deserve. Ibrahimovic finds Diaz in space on the left and the Colombian drives at Cash. As he enters the Villa box, Diaz cuts inside onto his preferred right foot and smashes a shot towards goal. It appeared to go right over Bizot, who opts not to put a hand up. The ball crashes off the underside of the bar and goes in. It has been all Bayern in this second half and that goal had been coming.

Bayern are knocking on the door and come very close to doubling their lead. Diaz’s shot from the edge of the box looks destined to hit the net with Bizot beaten but fortunately for Villa Abraham is on hand on his own goal line to make the block.

Bizot makes another great save. Bayern win a free-kick out on the right after Brown was fouled. Bischoff opts to shoot instead of crossing and nearly beats Bizot at his near post but the Aston Villa keeper gets across to his left to make the save.

Unai Emery makes a double substitution as Mings and Lynch replace Torres and Guessand. Mings takes the captain’s armband.

That is a fantastic double save from Bizot, first denying Stanisic and then Ibrahimovic. Both of those shots came through bodies so Bizot did a good job of reacting and making the saves with his legs on both occasions.

It is safe to say the Bayern fans out in Hong Kong love Diaz, who is cheered every time he touches the ball.

Vincent Kompany is going to make a triple change as Ito, Diaz and Palhinha come on. Former Liverpool man Diaz received a great ovation from the fans in Hong Kong. Palhinha, who spent last season on loan at Tottenha, has been linked with a move to Aston Villa in this window.

Should Bayern have been awarded a penalty there? A ball is played in behind the Villa defence into the penalty area and Ibrahimovic appeared to be brought down but the referee waves those appeals away. On first viewing, that appeared to be a penalty.

Just before the hour mark, it is time for some changes from Aston Villa. Abraham and Bogarde come on for Madjo and Kamara. This is Abraham’s first appearance of this pre-season.

Good play from Gomes earns Aston Villa a free-kick not far outside the Bayern penalty area out on the left, in a similar position to the free-kick that Bayern scored from in the first half. Buendia clips in a good ball to the back post, where Guessand looks likely to score but instead misses the ball on the stretch. Should Guessand have done better with that? Probably.

Brown was starting in his customary left-back position for Bayern in the first half but is now operating out on the right wing.

Gomes leaves one late on Pavlovic and, had this been a competitive fixture, I suspect that might have been a yellow card.

Tah is brought down by Gomes and Bayern will have a free-kick out on the right not a million miles outside the Villa penalty area. The delivery though is poor and easily cleared away.

Bayern have brought Stanisic on at half-time for Laimer. Aston Villa have not made a change at the break.

Possession: Aston Villa 45%-55% Bayern MunichShots: 4-7Shots on target: 1-2Corners: 1-2

The first half in Hong Kong is brought to an end and Bayern take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of Kim’s goal.

There will be one added minute at the end of this first half.

Aston Villa have struggled to create much going forward and have not really had a genuine goal-scoring opportunity in this first half. Their forward line though will look quite different when they kick off the seaosn than it does today.

The German side take the lead in Hong Kong. Bischof’s left-footed delivery from a free-kick out on the left is sublime, whipping it right into the corridor of uncertainty. The quality of delivery means it is quite a simple header for Kim, who makes no mistake with his header into the far corner. Kim might have been offside but obviously there is no VAR in use today. 1-0 Bayern.

That is a waste in the end from Bayern. Boey fires a pass in-field into Laimer, who takes a fantastic first touch on the turn inside the Villa half. He drives through the Villa half and at the penalty area but his pass outside looking for Cardozo is poor and overhit, with the ball rolling out for a goal kick. Laimer will be annoyed at himself having done all the hard work and then failed to execute the easy part.

Bischof eyes one up from range and tries to pick out the top corner. Bizot is routed to his spot and is hoping the shot goes wide. Bischof’s effort is always curling wide, much to Bizot’s relief.

The first booking of the game goes the way of Bayern Munich. Guessand drives forward into the Bayern half and is brought down by a cynical foul from Cardozo. You were half expecting Cardozo to perhaps escape without a booking with it being a pre-season friendly but he does not. It was the right call to book him.

That was lovely from Pavlovic. The German midfielder shows good feet to beat Gomes before getting his shot away from a central position just outside the box. He forces Bizot into a decent save but one he should be making.

Bayern force Villa into an error and win themselves a corner as a result out on the left. It is delivered into a dangerous area at the front post but Villa do a good job of handling it and clearing their lines.

Bayern Munich have made two signings this summer; Brown from Bundesliga rivals Frankfurt and Saibari from PSV. Brown is starting at left-back for Bayern today with Saibari not involved as he closes in on a return from a knock picked up at the World Cup with Morocco. Brown feels like such a Bayern signing, nabbing a good player from a Bundesliga rival.

Aston Villa have made four signings so far this summer but just one is in their starting XI today in the form of Gomes, who joined from Midlands rivals Wolves this summer. Young Swiss midfielder Manzambi has joined from Freiburg but is currently out injured. Garnacho picked up a knock and Cisse, who has arrived from LASK, is not involved for Villa today.

The ball is played in behind the Aston Villa defence to pick out the run of Binder. On the edge of the Villa box, Binder gets the first touch but Lindelof is calm in defence and heads back to his keeper Bizot.

Moments later, Gomes is dispossessed inside his own half and Ibrahimovic has a shot from just outside the box but drags it wide of the far post.

Good work from 17-year-old Madjo down Aston Villa’s left wins them their first corner of the game. Buendia’s inswinger is headed away too easily at the near post. Aston Villa have seen their former set-piece coach Austin MacPhee nabbed this summer by Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea.

The referee is allowing the game to flow and thus not blowing for soft fouls.

The first chance of the game falls to Bayern Munich. Brown’s cross from the left is headed by Maatsen straight to Ibrahimovic on the edge of the box. Ibrahimovic, not any relation to Zlatan, takes the shot on first time but it is blocked by Maatsen, who makes up for that poor header with the block. The ball goes behind for a corner, which comes to nothing.

Interestingly, there are only eight outfield substitutions on the Aston Villa bench for this game, with the likes of Garnacho and McGinn picking up knocks the other day. It appears then that at least a couple of Villa outfield players will have to play the full 90.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel, Aston Villa led out by Matty Cash and Bayern Munich by Manuel Neuer, and we are closing in on kick-off in Hong Kong. A group of delegates shake the hands of both starting XIs.

Chelsea and Juventus played in this stadium the other night and it is safe to say that the pitch does not look in the best state ahead of kick-off today. It looks like it will continue to rip up and the last thing the two managers will want is to pick up any serious injuries.

Currently, before the two sides emerge, the crowd in Hong Kong are being treated to some pre-match dancing and entertainment, which includes people dressed as pandas and sharks dancing. Would the Premier League ever take inspiration and have dancing pandas before kick-off?

Aston Villa: Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen, Kamara, Joao Gomes, Hemmings, Buendia, Guessand, Madjo.Substitutes: Wright, Asemota, Mings, Abraham, Nedejkovic, Bogarde, Rowe, Burrowes, Carroll, Lynch.

Bayern Munich: Neuer, Kim, Tah, Brown, Boey, Laimer, Bischof, Pavlovic, Ibrahimovic, Binder, Cardozo. Substitutes: Ulrich, Podar-Stiube, Urbig, Kimmich, Luis Díaz, Palhinha, Ito, Chávez, Pavic, Bara, Manuba, Stanisic, Della Rovere, Assomo.

The likes of Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa and Emi Martinez are yet to return to training after their World Cup exploits and Aston Villa are also without captain John McGinn and new signing Alejandro Garnacho, who picked up knocks in their win over BG Pathum the other day.

Aston Villa have already sold Youri Tielemans and Morgan Rogers this summer, with Lucas Digne on the verge of a move to PSG, but could another starter be on the way out of Villa Park? England defender Ezri Konsa has been linked with moves to the likes of Arsenal and Liverpool but will Unai Emery be able to keep hold of the 28-year-old?

The atmosphere is building with our fans in Hong Kong! 🔴⚪️#AudiFCBTour pic.twitter.com/m4fFXAWxGb

It has been a big summer of change at Aston Villa already and there could be more changes before the end of the window. Left-back Lucas Digne is set to move to PSG and is set to be replaced by Atlético Madrid’s Matteo Ruggeri. Joao Palhinha, who is on the bench for Bayern Munich today, has been linked with a move to Aston Villa.

“Aston Villa are a top side with a very good coach. They have a large squad and will field plenty of talent. They have already played more friendlies than us, but for us it is a good challenge. It is a match in which we will learn a lot about our team’s fitness. It will be a good match for us.”

“It is difficult to improve; after all, it is not just about the trophies we have won, but also about the number of goals and matches we have won. It is possible, but difficult. Right now, I would say our aim is to win the Champions League; there is no doubt about that. And throughout the season, I will be saying that we need to focus on the next match. Aston Villa’s preparations for the new season continue out in Hong Kong as they take on Bundesliga champions Bayern Munich at the Kai Tak Stadium. These sides have met twice before; Aston Villa beat Bayern 1-0 to win the European Cup in 1981/82 before then meeting in the Champions League group stages during the 2024/25 season, with Jhon Duran’s long-range screamer giving Aston Villa a 1-0 win at Villa Park.

After losing two of their first three pre-season friendlies, Aston Villa have won their first two games on Asian soil and this game marks the end of their tour of the Far East. It has been a summer of significant change at Aston Villa thus far with some key members of their squad departing and some new faces arriving. Youri Tielemans has departed after Manchester United triggered his release clause and they then sold Morgan Rogers to Chelsea for a British transfer record £117m. Unai Emery’s side have brought in 20-year-old Swiss midfielder Johan Manzambi, Brazilian midfielder Joao Gomes and Alejandro Garnacho, with the deal for Garnacho being an initial loan. Manzambi is currently on the sidelines due to a knee injury.

Unai Emery’s side were dealt a blow during the World Cup as Belgian midfielder Amadou Onana picked up a serious knee injury. They were though boosted by the return of Boubacar Kamara after seven months out as he scored in the 3-1 friendly victory over BG Parthum. As one midfielder returned from injury in that game, another picked up a fresh injury as John McGinn suffered a knock to his knee. The likes of Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa and Emi Martinez are yet to return after their world Cup exploits. They begin their Premier League campaign with an away game on the south coast against Brighton on August 23 but will be involved in the Uefa Super Cup against PSG next week having lifted the Europa League last season.

Bayern Munich head into this season looking to win a third straight Bundesliga title and have won two of their three friendlies, losing once. They have added Moroccan attacker Ismael Saibari from PSV and German left-back Nathaniel Brown from Bundesliga rivals Eintracht Frankfurt to their ranks this summer. The likes of Harry Kane, Dayot Upamecano and Michael Olise are not available as they are still yet to return after World Cup duty but Vincent Kompany has confirmed that Bayern’s German stars are set to return.

After today, Bayern have one more friendly against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

#1993. Dida discusses Endrick rumours, Torriani’s growth and ‘great coach’ Amorim

Nelson Dida believes that Ruben Amorim is showing he is a ‘great’ coach, and he gave his take on the Endrick to AC Milan rumours.

If anyone knows about the pressure of playing for Milan, it is Dida. Having been at the club from 2000 to 2010, he made over 300 official appearances for the Rossoneri and was part of an era that brought in eight major trophies under Carlo Ancelotti.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

He is widely regarded as one of the finest goalkeepers of his generation and was decisive in the 2003 Champions League final penalty shootout against Juventus. He also returned briefly as a goalkeeping coach, working for a year with Maignan.

Dida spoke to reporters who were present at the Galbiati Trophy and he answered a few questions regarding his former team, with his words relayed by MilanNews.

“Amorim is proving to be a great coach. He took over Milan and is having a fantastic season. I think the attention is right because at Milan you can never make mistakes, but he has the ability to keep the team together to do well in the league.”

If Maignan is hurt, would you come back and put the gloves on?

“We already have a goalkeeper at AC Milan: Lorenzo Torriani, a guy who’s doing well. I like him. Last year, too, he did well when he had opportunities. I think he’s a focused guy, if he gets more opportunities, he can continue to grow.”

“Milan are slowly growing. They’re doing well in the league, I think we can still do more, while in Europe we’re still missing something.”

“Endrick is a great player for me. When I see him play, he looks a bit like Romario, who is a bit small, but when he’s in the penalty area, he’s decisive. When he’s had the opportunity to play, he’s also scored goals.

“I think he can really do well for Real Madrid and the national team, but I don’t know if he’s available to join Milan. I hope a Brazilian returns to play in the Italian league soon and wears the Milan shirt.”

#1992. Barnsley FC 1 Sheffield Wednesday 2: Headstart costs Reds against clinical Owls

On a night dedicated to Weston Park's cancer work, the Reds extended that charity to their defending, and within 15 minutes, Wednesday already looked uncatchable.

Vimal Yoganathan's sixth goal in eight games ensured a proper South Yorkshire derby broke out, but the Reds are getting rather too good at nearly or semi-performances for their own comfort down in the League One relegation zone.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

After Yoganathan's strike, the home side showed the fight they should be a given in games against the near-neighbours, but it was already too late.

For the visitors, it was a character test passed in front of 5,700 invigilators in the away end, Jamal Lowe scoring from their only two shots on target on a night that felt like a big step forward for their new manager, Dave Challinor.

"Three points away ole, ole," sang the packed away end and more pertinently, "Wednesday are back."

Funny how one week can totally change the mood of a football club.

The Reds actually started the better, but they are getting good at looking good in ineffectual parts of the field, and awful at the business ends.

Their fans had been in mutinous mood before the game, hundreds gathering outside the ground before kick-off to protest about the way things are being run, but there was no such defiance when they needed it early on.

Lowe – playing more of an orthodox winger role with the balance of Wednesday's unchanged side titled more towards a back four than a three than it had been the previous week – was ruthless in exploiting it.

When Barry Bannan lofted a free-kick to the back post in the ninth minute, Liam Cooper was in far too much space there. The defender headed the ball across goal, and Lowe pounced for the Owls' third set-piece goal in a week.

Five minutes later, two passes took the visitors from the halfway line to a second goal.

Callum Slattery's pass to Bannan was almost cut out but when he found Lowe, but Jubril Okedina stood off, almost daring the forward to score, so he did.

Barnsley's early work lacked that conviction.

Reyes Cleary's second-minute snapshot lacked the power to beat Joe Lumley, and Ryan Brownlie's also allowed the goalkeeper to save. Makenzie Kirk miskicked a shot when Cleary picked him out, and when Patrick Kelly ran onto a knockdown by the centre-forward, his shot lacked power.

Cleary put a shot well wide and Luca Connell hammered one into Billy Mitchell.

Ziyad Larkeche controlled a fairly routine Cieran Slicker pass over the touchline.

But a side with seven starters under the age of 23 plugged away and got back into it courtesy of one of their young leaders.

Like Okedina, Yan Valery stood off Cleary and when the winger delivered a low cross, Yoganathan arrived onto it like a centre-forward to pull a goal back.

With both sides attacking their own noisy ends, it made for an entertaining second half.

Like Barnsley at the start of the first half, Wednesday pushed the harder, without making it count.

Bannan had a shot blocked and when Slicker came out of his goal to stop former Red Davis Keillor-Dunn finishing a Bannan pass, Lowe lifted his shot onto the roof of the net.

At the other end, Barnsley centre-back Sam Gale forced his way to the byline, but his cross cleared those in the area. Larkeche put an acrobatic effort wide.

It was Wednesday who were throwing on the substitutes - a sign of their deeper resources, but also off their keenness to finally add to Lowe's second shot on target, 14 minutes in.

Despite one of those substitutes, Harry Gray, accelerating past Gale for a chance Slattery had blocked, it never came, but it did not need to because hard as Barnsley pushed – throwing centre-back Connor O'Riordan on as a late emergency striker and sending Slicker up for a stoppage-time corner – they could not find the next goal either.

Luca Connell came the closest, his free-kick tipped over in the 93rd minute.

His team are just not good enough to gift promotion wannabes like Wednesday a two-goal headstart and get away with it. Only just, you might say, but game after game that is enough.

Barnsley: Slicker; Okedina (Reid 86), Gale, Kay, Larkeche; Connell, Kelly (Johnson 86); Brownlie (O'Riordan 90), Yoganathan (Noslin 81), Cleary; Kirk (Toure 81).

Sheffield Wednesday: Lumley; Valery, Bernard (Santos 86), Cooper, Swinkels (Palmer 70); Heskey, Mitchell (Barry 70), Slattery, Bannan (Gray 78), J Lowe (Liongola 70); Keillor-Dunn.

#1990. Dave Challinor on why he thought Sheffield Wednesday's early lead backfired against Barnsley FC

Two goals inside the opening quarter of an hour from Jamal Lowe ought to have seen the Owls to a comfortable victory over opponents who have now not won in ten League One games.

But they did not have another shot on target all night, and were made to sweat it out on a freezing cold night to claim a 2-1 victory.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

"You've always got to work hard," said Challinor, who was taking charge of his first League One away game as Owls manager.

"The players probably felt we didn't work hard enough in the first half. After going after going in front, sometimes it's the worst thing can happen because players think the game's done and we can now sit back and not have to have to defend with the personnel we've got on the pitch.

"Us defending in a block with looking to break with Slatts (Callum Slattery) and Davis (Keillor-Dunn) and Barry Bannan doesn't really work for us, so we need to be more aggressive, high up the pitch, and expose ourselves. We didn't do that, it'll take time.

"I'll own that in terms of what it looks like but that's where we need to get to.

"We've got to at that point really be on the neck of people and go and get the third goal, not be comfortable thinking two is an easy night for us because you allow a young team to get some momentum and come back into the game."

But as critical as he was of areas of the first-half performance, Challinor was delighted with the spirt he saw in his new players in the second half.

"We've got we've got a group that want to defend right across the board," he said. "We've done some work this week around emergency defending.

"You're not going to get much better than Coops (Liam Cooper), Sil (Swinkels), Dish (Di'Shon Bernard), Yan (Valery) and Rico (Ricardo Santos).

"They want to block, they want to get themselves in the way.

"We were a little bit better second half.

"We had a really good chat at half time. I told them what I felt, we'd just got to make better decisions.

"We've got we've got an experienced group, but some of our decision-making in that last half an hour caused us more problems than it should have.

"If it's a derby, you need to be able to be 100 per cent because Barnsley, at that point, are going for it, are open, and two or three passes, we could have we could have been in a lot more often, and we made the wrong decision at the wrong time.

"Winning's a brilliant habit, but I'm very realistic about the work that needs to be done.

"I never have been a great winner, as daft as that sounds. My job's to be analytical and understand where we get better.

"I want them to enjoy winning. I've said that to them. I want it to be absolutely bouncing because winning's a brilliant feeling and a brilliant habit to get into.

"They found a way when maybe not performed the best. There's loads more to come from this group. My job is to make sure that happens.

"You're always going to be try and be a perfectionist as a football coach. You'll never get to that but that doesn't mean you stop trying."

It left coach Stendel downbeat when he addressed the media after the game.

When asked if he thought the first 15 minutes had decided the game, Stendel replied: "I would wouldn't say the first 15 minutes was two situations, and I know you would think, 'What you do in training?' but we talked exactly that about this, especially the second goal after last week.

"But yeah, when you do not defend the ball with the last desire, then you concede a goal like this, and this was hard.

"The support was really good but 2-0 down after 15 minutes in a game like this is hard against a team with so much quality.

"After the second goal, we have the feeling only we played in the game but we only scored one goal, and we talk again about the defeat in the game that we don't have to lose."

"Everybody can see that the players never give up, we really have a good character in the squad, a lot of power, and we can play at 2-0 down against one from the top teams in the league.

"We lose by only on one goal a lot of times.

"It showed we have a good mentality in the group, but everybody - not only the players, not only supporters, everybody needs a positive result in the league."

#1983. Man City midfielder tipped for free transfer exit as preferred destinations emerge

By Naim Beneddra | 19 Nov 2026 20:47

Manchester City could lose an experienced midfielder on a free transfer at the end of the season, with fresh reports suggesting that the player has already identified the European leagues in which he would prefer to continue his career.

Mateo Kovacic is expected to leave the Etihad Stadium when his contract expires in June 2027, according to transfer journalist Matteo Moretto, who has also provided an update on the Croatia international's preferred destinations.

Speaking to Marca, Moretto claimed that the 32-year-old would welcome a return to Spain or Italy, where he previously represented Real Madrid and Inter Milan respectively.

"He will leave City at the end of the season," Moretto said, before explaining that Kovacic "would like to return to Spain or Italy", although his salary expectations could influence his options.

The update comes as Kovacic struggles to secure regular playing time under Enzo Maresca, having fallen down the midfield pecking order since the Italian replaced Pep Guardiola.

While City have not officially announced his departure, the midfielder is approaching the final seven months of his contract without a reported agreement over an extension.

Kovacic joined Manchester City from Chelsea in June 2023, signing a four-year contract in a deal worth an initial £25m, with a further £5m potentially payable in add-ons.

The Croatia international was recruited to provide experience, technical quality and composure in midfield, having previously enjoyed considerable success with both Real Madrid and Chelsea.

However, injuries have increasingly disrupted his time in Manchester.

The midfielder was restricted to just nine appearances during the 2025-26 campaign after undergoing surgery to address a troublesome heel problem.

Although he has returned to action this season, his opportunities have remained limited under Maresca.

Kovacic has made eight appearances across all competitions, contributing one goal and one assist, but only one of those outings has been a Premier League start.

He has also been used sparingly in the Champions League, with the manager preferring other midfield options for the majority of City's European fixtures.

His two full appearances in the EFL Cup underline the change in his status, although he was entrusted with the captain's armband in one of those matches.

The situation represents a considerable shift for a player who has won four Champions League titles and previously played an important role in some of Europe's most successful teams.

Reports linking Kovacic with an exit have circulated for several months.

In September, the Croatian was reportedly considering a January departure after becoming frustrated with his lack of opportunities.

Moretto's latest information, however, points towards a summer move when Kovacic would become available without a transfer fee.

From January, the midfielder will be eligible to negotiate a pre-contract agreement with clubs outside England, potentially allowing him to arrange his next destination before the end of the campaign.

Kovacic's reported preference for Spain or Italy would represent a return to familiar surroundings rather than an entirely new challenge.

The midfielder spent two seasons with Inter Milan before joining Real Madrid in 2015, where he won three consecutive Champions League titles between 2016 and 2018.

He subsequently moved to Chelsea, initially on loan, and spent five seasons at Stamford Bridge before completing his switch to City.

His experience in Serie A has already attracted attention from Italian clubs.

Juventus were linked with a move for Kovacic in September, when reports suggested that the Turin giants had identified him as one of several potential free-agent signings for the summer of 2027.

The Bianconeri were also said to be monitoring Fikayo Tomori and David Raum as part of their efforts to strengthen the squad without paying substantial transfer fees.

AC Milan have separately been mentioned among Kovacic's possible suitors, although there is no indication that either Italian club has reached an agreement with the player.

The possibility of returning to La Liga also remains open, but Moretto's comments did not identify a Spanish club currently negotiating for his signature.

His wages could prove the biggest obstacle to a move.

Despite the prospect of securing an accomplished international without paying City a transfer fee, interested clubs would still need to reach an agreement over a salary package acceptable to Kovacic.

For City, the latest update raises the prospect of losing another member of Guardiola's former midfield without receiving a transfer fee.

Maresca's current selection decisions suggest that Kovacic is no longer regarded as an automatic starter, although the Croatian remains part of the squad and has not publicly confirmed any plans to leave.

With his contract due to expire next June, the coming months could determine whether he completes his final season in Manchester or attracts an offer to bring forward his departure.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

The west London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

Chelsea had further chances to extend their lead in a dominant second-half performance but were unable to add to their three goals.

Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge before beginning their Premier League campaign at Fulham.

AC Milan take on Amorim’s former club Manchester United next Saturday before they kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

Chelsea managed to lure Austin MacPhee to take care of their set-pieces and today Chelsea scored two goals from corners. Here is a snippet of Mike McGrath’s piece on MacPhee’s arrival at Chelsea:

He is among the new breed of coaches who are rock stars in their own right, taking centre-stage since rules were changed so that only one person is allowed in the technical area at a time. For MacPhee to get closer to the players for a set-piece, it will mean Xabi Alonso taking a step back onto the bench.

It has been an incredible rise for MacPhee, 46, who was working on Michael O’Neill’s staff with Northern Ireland 10 years ago this summer, helping them reach the knockout stages of the European Championship.

Chelsea take on Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia tomorrow before returning to the UK. Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad before taking on Fulham on the opening weekend of the new season.

AC Milan will play Manchester United next weekend and then kick off their Serie A campaign against Torino.

Xabi Alonso is going to make his first two changes of the game as Jackson and Quenda replace Welbeck and Neto.

Chelsea have their third and their new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee will be delighted with that one. Lavia plays a flat delivery from a corner out on the left to Caicedo on the edge of the box. Caicedo hits it first time on the volley with the outside of his right foot and picks out the bottom right corner with perfection.

Chelsea go 2-0 up not even a minute into the second half. Neto, on the right side of the box, cuts onto his preferred left foot and crosses to the far post. Pedro gets on the end of it and, despite the Milan keeper getting a touch on the shot, the ball ends up in the far corner.

AC Milan have made a raft of changes at the break, which includes their new record signing Ramos, who has joined from PSG this summer. Former Chelsea man Nkunku is also on. Milan were back out from the dressing rooms a fair bit earlier than Chelsea were. The first half in Jakarta is brought an end and Chelsea take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of Pedro’s goal on the stroke of half-time.

90 seconds into added time at the end of this first half, we have the first goal in Jakarta. Pedro really should not have been afforded so much space in the six-yard box.

As Leao approaches the Chelsea box, Leao attempts to push it past Acheampong but the young Chelsea defender times his sliding challenge to perfection and puts it behind for a corner. Sanchez punches it out to the edge of the box, where Comotto takes it on his chest before volleying towards goal. The ball goes behind for another corner, which Chelsea just about scramble away.

Chelsea hit the post. Palestra drives forward for Chelsea down their left before the ball falls to Welbeck on the left side of the box. Welbeck’s effort hits the outside of the post. AC Milan keeper Torriani appeared though to always have it covered.

Caicedo’s inswinging delivery is headed away at the front post.

We are under way in Jakarta, Indonesia, in Chelsea’s penultimate game over in the Far East. Before the game started, a huge AC Milan tifo was unveiled at one end of the ground.

It is 7pm in Jakarta yet the temperature is still up at 29 degrees with the humidity at nearly 70%. These conditions will be a proper test for both sides.

The teams emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off in Indonesia.

The trophies won by Franco Baresi, who has died at the age of 66, are their own monument to the AC Milan and Italy defender’s greatness. Six times a Serie A champion, five as captain, three European Cup-winning campaigns, 10 other winners’ medals and the distinction of being a member of Italy squads that finished in first, second and third places at World Cup tournaments demonstrate that his career, in a significantly more meritocratic era, stand alongside the giants even if the bias towards attacking virtuosos denied him the Ballon d’Or his talent deserved.

Yet they do not tell us why the grief, so tangible in Milan and beyond today, transcends tribal rivalry. It would be unfair to say that he transformed the art of Italian defending. Gaetano Scirea, the elegant Juventus sweeper who kept the 21-year-old Baresi confined to the bench when Italy won their third World Cup in 1982, had a surplus of natural ability, composure and intelligence. He did not need the raw-elbowed brutality of Claudio Gentile, heir to generations of Italian defenders influenced by the post-war influx of players brought up in the traditions of Argentina and Uruguay.

Chelsea’s pre-season continues out in the Far East as they take on AC Milan in the Gelora Bung Karno Stadium in Jakarta, Indonesia. Both clubs now have new managers, with Xabi Alonso taking over at Chelsea and former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim now at the helm at AC Milan. These sides met in pre-season last year, with Chelsea winning 4-1 at Stamford Bridge. At that time, now-Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca was in charge whilst Max Allegri, who is now at Napoli, was leading AC Milan. The last time they met competitively was during the 2022/23 Champions League season, with Chelsea winning both games.

Chelsea lost 1-0 to AC Milan’s Serie A rivals Juventus on Wednesday in Hong Kong, in which Danny Welbeck made his first Chelsea appearance after joining from Brighton in the last week.

“We want to have a great team spirit and that is built on a daily basis with a great culture in the building,” Alonso said in his pre-match press conference. “That helps in the moment you have to compete. You feel better having that togetherness, trust, and the bonds between the players are so important to ultimately building a winning mentality, and a team that can compete anywhere. So the football side is so important, but the mental side is as important. And the strength of the team is the most important. We have been able to train and prepare [during pre-season] and I am very happy with the attitude and personality, we know that it is a very important part of this tour.”

It has been another busy week on the transfer front for Chelsea; not only has Welbeck arrived over the last week but so too have Jordan Henderson and Valentin Barco. Alonso’s men have two more games after this against Johor Darul Ta’zim and Real Sociedad before getting their Premier League campaign under way with a derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage.

AC Milan finished fifth in Serie A last season to earn a spot in the Europa League last season. Their big-money acquisition this summer as been Portuguese striker Goncalo Ramos from PSG. They have played two pre-season friendlies so far, which have both ended in draws; 2-2 against Celtic and then 1-1 against city rivals Inter. They kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

#1981. Eli Junior Kroupi stance on Arsenal transfer revealed as Bournemouth make decision for January window

Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi is targeting a move outside of the Premier League despite interest from Arsenal, Chelsea, Manchester City and Tottenham, according to reports.

Kroupi joined Bournemouth in a £12 million deal from French side Lorient last year and scored 13 goals in his first season in the Premier League.

The 20-year-old has suffered a disrupted start to the new campaign as he required surgery on a foot injury sustained during a pre-season training session in Austria in July.

Kroupi returned in Bournemouth’s 3-0 win away to Manchester United on October 25 and has made three more appearances as a substitute for Marco Rose’s side.

During the international break, Kroupi was handed his senior debut for France as he featured in the 3-1 defeat to Italy, as well as in the 2-1 win over Turkey.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

The French striker has attracted interest from Arsenal, Chelsea and Tottenham, while Paris Saint-Germain, Bayern Munich and Barcelona have also been monitoring his progress in the Premier League.

However, David Ornstein has claimed that Kroupi will look to move overseas when he leaves Bournemouth, although the club are not looking to sell the forward in the January transfer window.

‘There was a big story recently about Alex Scott possibly leaving in the January transfer window, that was conditional on Bournemouth receiving £100 million and being in a really strong position in the Premier League where that becomes a bit of a no-brainer because in six months’ time he’ll have a year to go on his contract and it’s a very different conversation,’ Ornstein said on The Athletic FC’s podcast.

‘Kroupi has got much longer on his contract for a start, so there’s no massive need to sell in a way you would consider selling Scott.

‘He’s been out injured for longer as well, so I think Bournemouth want to make use of him this season and they don’t think their chances of recouping significant value in the summer will be much worse than in January, probably better actually.

‘My information around Kroupi is he would like to move at some point, outside of England.

‘You’ve seen very heavy reporting around PSG and Barcelona. If he continues to show the level of form that he was displaying prior to his injury, the biggest clubs in world football want him.

‘It’s no surprise he’s high up on Premier League club recruitment lists, but if what I’m hearing to date is anything to go by, those Premier League clubs may be disappointed because he could be travelling back to warmer climes.’

#1980. Romano: Balde expected to leave Barcelona – Milan’s position after summer talks

AC Milan have been linked with a move for Alejandro Balde, but Fabrizio Romano claims some flexibility is needed from Barcelona.

In the past couple of weeks there has been more talk about Milan strengthening in the left-back role. Pervis Estupinan has not been convincing since his arrival, while Davide Bartesaghi and Diego Moreira have been used further forward in recent weeks.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Yunus Musah was even adapted to playing as a left-sided defender in the recent win over Genoa, so it’s clear that Ruben Amorim might welcome a more natural player for the role, one that fits his ideas of how to play.

In a video on his YouTube channel, Fabrizio Romano touched upon a number of different topics connected to Milan, from Francesco Camarda’s fate to the possibility of a young midfielder arriving. He also spoke about Balde – another recent link – and his words are via MilanNews.

“Balde is a name that can be a key player in January. Then, to be completely honest, he’s a foreign transfer name, being realistic. He earns more than €5 million net per season,” he began.

“Barcelona were willing to let him go in the summer, but wanted a permanent deal worth €50-55 million. As for Italy, despite Mendes also trying to see if there was any room for negotiation with Milan, there were never any real negotiations. Also because the costs are decidedly high.

“Balde still isn’t playing and will speak with Mendes today, who is on a mission to Barcelona to meet with the player and his family and figure out what to do in the January transfer window.

“I’d keep an eye on the possibility if the formula were to change, because these are currently foreign figures. But he’s a player to keep an eye on. We’ll see if he goes to Italy or abroad.”

#1979. ‘Back-up is needed’ - Leeds United told their ‘next step’ in recruitment by Premier League icon Michael Owen

Premier League icon Michael Owen believes the signing of a forward should be the “next step” for Leeds United.

Leeds signed Dominic Calvert-Lewin on a free transfer from Everton in the summer of 2025 and he has since led the line to widespread acclaim. His form has pushed him back into the England fold and he recently picked up his 15th cap in a 3-2 Nations League win over Spain.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Lukas Nmecha was recruited in the same summer and is the second-choice frontman, with Joel Piroe now out on loan at West Ham United.

Leeds are not blessed with a lengthy list of alternatives to the pair and Owen believes depth will be key if the Whites are to keep climbing the Premier League table.

He told The Yorkshire Post: “Calvert-Lewin looks to have a new lease of life playing for Leeds and is doing a good job and playing well.

“But for Leeds to keep building and improving, having back-up is needed as they have started the season well and [they are] looking competitive in games I’ve seen this season for sure.

“They’ve recruited well with James Trafford, so yes, another striker would be the next step for sure.”

The likes of Harry Wilson, Noah Okafor and Jean-Matteo Bahoya could deployed up front, but their presence in that role would require a system change.

Piroe was once Leeds’ chief marksman but does not appear to have a future at Elland Road, nor does Wilfried Gnonto, who is now on loan at Fiorentina.

Leeds boss Daniel Farke could well want another option in the ‘number nine’ department, but persuading a player to be a third-choice option is not an easy task.

#1978. Bournemouth vs Nottingham Forest - prediction, team news, lineups

By Oliver Thomas | 19 Nov 2026 21:00, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 09:24

Eyeing up a place in the top four of the Premier League, in-form Bournemouth welcome Nottingham Forest to the Vitality Stadium on Saturday afternoon.

The spoils were shared in the last meeting between these two teams in May, with an opener from Forest star Morgan Gibbs-White cancelled out in the second half by Cherries attacker Marcus Tavernier to rescue a 1-1 draw.

Bournemouth’s 2026-27 campaign started with just two wins in eight matches across all competitions (D3 L3), including no victories in six Premier League fixtures, but the Cherries have since put together an impressive eight-game winning streak under new boss Marco Rose.

A slender 2-1 success at Ipswich Town prior to the international break helped them climb up to seventh in the Premier League table, just three points behind Liverpool in fourth, and they are now aiming to win five straight top-flight games for the first time in their history.

Since the start of October, Bournemouth have scored more goals across all competitions than any other Premier League team (22), netting at least two goals in each game during their eight-match winning run.

In-form striker Evanilson has been Bournemouth's driving force, with the Brazilian’s goal against Ipswich making him the first Cherries player to score in five successive PL matches. He also has the joint-most top-flight goal involvements this season (nine - five goals, four assists), level with Erling Haaland (nine goals).

Not only do Bournemouth enter Saturday’s contest having never lost in eight previous Premier League battles with Nottingham Forest (W4 D4), but Rose has also won his last four meetings with teams managed by Oliver Glasner (all in the Bundesliga between 2021 and 2023).

After enduring a sluggish start to life under Glasner, winning just one of their first nine Premier League games, Nottingham Forest entered the international break on a massive high after securing a statement 3-1 victory over Manchester City at the City Ground – their first home league win of the campaign.

Liam Delap ended a five-game goal drought with a superb brace against his former club that followed an earlier opener from Jair Cunha, with Forest scoring more goals in this match (three) than they had in their previous six home league fixtures combined (two).

Sitting 16th in the Premier League table and one point above the drop zone, Forest must now translate that momentum onto their travels, having failed to keep an away clean sheet in the top flight since April while losing their last two games on the road against Crystal Palace (3-1) and Brentford (2-0).

Although Forest have scored the second-fewest goals in the division this term (nine), Glasner – who takes charge of his 100th Premier League match on Saturday – will hope that his team’s clinical display against Man City signals a turning point after weeks of frustration in front of goal.

The Tricky Trees head to the Vitality Stadium seeking to win back-to-back league games for only the second time this calendar year, but they are winless in six away league encounters against Bournemouth (D2 L4).

Bournemouth duo Alex Toth (thigh) and Juanlu Sanchez (ankle) remain sidelined with injuries, while Julian Araujo is still nursing a thigh problem and is unlikely to be involved this weekend.

Rayan sustained a knock on international duty with Brazil, but the winger should be fit to start on the right side of attack, linking up with Justin Kluivert, Marcus Tavernier and red-hot centre-forward Evanilson.

Eli Junior Kroupi is another attacking option pushing to start having made a full recovery from injury and scoring his first goal for France last weekend, while in-demand midfielder Alex Scott is available to start for the first time since suffering a thigh injury with England in October.

As for Nottingham Forest, Nicolas Dominguez (hamstring) remains a long-term absentee and has been joined in the treatment room by Callum Hudson-Odoi (groin), while Neco Williams (ankle) and Xaver Schlager (thigh) have both emerged as doubts after picking up injuries with Wales and Austria respectably over the international break.

Nicolo Savona is yet to play for Forest this season due to a knee injury, but he is back training and may be in a position to return to the matchday squad. A start is seemingly unlikely, though, with Daniel Munoz and either Williams - if fit - or Luca Netz expected to start as wing-backs.

Delap is bidding to score in successive PL games for the first time since April 2025 with Ipswich and is expected to lead the line once again, with Gibbs-White and Dan Ndoye potentially providing support in advanced positions; the latter’s inclusion would allow James McAtee to move back into a deeper midfield position.

Petrovic; Smith, Hill, Silva, Truffert; Adams, Cook; Rayan, Kluivert, Tavernier; Evanilson

Nottingham Forest possible starting lineup:

Sels; Cunha, Milenkovic, Murillo; Munoz, McAtee, Schlager, Williams; Ndoye, Gibbs-White; Delap

Both Bournemouth and Forest enter this contest in buoyant mood as they look to build on positive results prior to the international break.

Although six of Forest's last seven Premier League away games have seen both teams score, we are backing the Cherries to frustrate an opponent they have historically enjoyed facing and secure three more points without reply to extend their impressive winning run to nine matches.

#1977. Chelsea told to sign £60million Arsenal star instead of Alex Scott

Chelsea should drop their interest in Bournemouth star Alex Scott and turn their attention to a more experienced alternative, according to Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink.

The Blues invested heavily in their squad again during the summer transfer window, but remain light in central midfield where they are heavily reliant on Moises Caicedo following the departures of Enzo Fernandez and Andrey Santos.

Romeo Lavia’s return to form and fitness has represented a welcome boost, but Xabi Alonso is keen to reinforce his engine room further come January.

Scott, who Chelsea attempted to sign in the summer, could well be on the move given his delicate contract situation at Bournemouth.

Arsenal and Liverpool have both been linked with the England international and although Hasselbaink is a keen admirer of the 23-year-old, he feels his old club would be better suited by targeting the Gunners’ out of favour Spain international Martin Zubimendi.

‘If they can go out and get Martin Zubimendi from Arsenal, then they should absolutely go and get him.  Go and get him in January. He’s not playing at the moment at Arsenal, but he will make Chelsea stronger.

#1976. Sergej Jakirovic on Hull City taking a risk following Brighton and Hove Albion blueprint

The Seagulls started the 21st Century in English football's fourth tier with no history of challenging at the top of the pyramid and no home, but are now second in the Premier League, fifth in the Europa Conference League and looking good for it. They will come to East Yorkshire on Sunday looking to end Hull's unbeaten start to the season at home.

Although they have not won since August, the Tigers are also punching above their weight, 13th in the Premier League and crucially with more points than games played after coming up via the play-offs.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Hull signed 18 players in the summer, 14 of whom were under the age of 25, and another 14 new to the Premier League.

“We have to speak about them because it is not now by accident,” said Hull coach Jakirovic. “They are performing even better every game.

“They have very big confidence, an excellent coach (Fabian Hurzeler), system. This club has a spine and very good players – young players with potential.

“If your energy is below 100 per cent you don't have a chance against them.

“They sold a few good players but they have good scouting. They always bring in young potential players. They pay money for them, then they try to develop these players and then sell again. It is a great system.”

“Sometimes you cannot afford better players, more expensive players, but I think that we brought young players with good potential,” he said.

“Now it's about developing and how we can improve them because this is a very big step for some of them.

“Especially if you stay in the league, then you have more money, you can invest, you can add more quality players.

“It's about vision. It's about strategy. This is everything with Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth – they showed already how one club who is new in the league can be successful.

“This is maybe an example of what we need to do.”

Not many of Hull's new 18 have made much impact in the Premier League – yet. Some were always going to take time, and others will not come off at all.

“We have some examples here who joined us too late after pre-season, then you start to play,” acknowledged Jakirovic. “(You pick up) one injury, recovery, second injury. Now it's difficult to get back into the team – especially the first XI.

“They need time and they have to be patient and work very hard every day. So this is risky.”

Nobel Mendy is fit again after an international break where Hull had a large number of players representing their countries, and Jakirovic watching closely to see how they performed.

“We had 12 players in the building (during the break),” he said. “But we had two good sessions before Thursday when we were finally all together. everyone got back healthy.

“Now it's about fatigue, it's about condition. On Saturday we will decide who will play.

“I tried to watch every game (his internationals played) and if I cannot watch, Josh (Marris, senior analyst) will put it on our computer. Even Qatar v Australia (which centre-back Lucas Herrington played in), even under-21 games, Greece, Norway, with Jens (Hjerto-Dahl).”
